declarations.description:
A canvas stand-in that hides its display surface. Consumers draw into an
`OffscreenCanvas` through `getContext`, and a real `<canvas>` in a closed
shadow root is blitted from that bitmap.

`data-width` and `data-height` size the inner (logical) canvas. The outer
canvas can magnify each logical pixel into a cell: `data-scale` sets the
cell size in CSS pixels (default 1), `data-gap` the space between cells
(default 0), and `data-shape` the cell form, inscribed in the cell:
`"square"` (default), `"circle"`, `"ring"`, `"diamond"`, `"hex"` (pointy
top, odd rows half a cell right), `"triangle"` (two cells wide, up and down
by turns, interlocking), `"dash"` (a horizontal capsule),
`"slash"` (bottom left to top right) or `"cross"`. With the defaults the
outer canvas is a straight 1:1 mirror. A page can instead size cells from
CSS by setting `--emulated-canvas-scale` to a length on the element, which
then follows viewport changes without any script.

Gaps and the rest of each cell outside its shape are painted over the
cells rather than cut out, in `--emulated-canvas-gap-color` (default
`Canvas`, the page's default background); set it to whatever shows behind
the element. A pixel shadow is cast from square cells whatever the shape.

`data-shadow` (0–100, default 0) casts each pixel's shadow, like an LCD's
segments over their backplate: each pixel darkens what lies under it by how
much darker it is than unlit, at that opacity, offset by `data-shadow-x` and
`data-shadow-y` (whole CSS pixels, default 0). With a palette unlit is its
base, so only pixels darker than the base cast a shadow; without one it is
white. The shadow is cast from the frame's pixels on each present, so a
shadow over drawing other than a whole-bitmap `putImageData`, with no pass
on, reads the bitmap back.

Effects are `SHADERS`, an ordered list of per-pixel passes (a drifting
noise, a two-colour palette and an LCD's ghosting), each documenting its own
live `data-*` knobs in `shaders/`. They run on the logical bitmap, never at
display resolution, so each costs the same however large the cells are
drawn.

The canvas presents on its own, the way a plain `<canvas>` shows what is
drawn on it: drawing through the 2D context queues a present for when the
drawing code returns, so a frame drawn in an animation frame shows in that
same frame, and several calls cost one present. While a pass is still
changing the display, the canvas keeps presenting every animation frame, or
at about 8 fps for a pass that only drifts, then stops. `data-manual` opts
out: the owner calls `present()` itself.

The context is the inner canvas's own, with only its pixel-writing methods
wrapped to note that the bitmap changed: nothing is proxied or replayed, so
drawing costs what it costs on any canvas. A `putImageData` of the whole
bitmap hands the passes those pixels, sparing them a read-back; any other
drawing is read back once, on the present after it.
declarations.name: EmulatedCanvas

cssProperties.description: A length that sizes the cells instead of `data-scale`, so they follow the viewport without script.
cssProperties.name: --emulated-canvas-scale

cssProperties.description: Paints the gaps and the rest of each cell outside its shape.
cssProperties.name: --emulated-canvas-gap-color

members.name: width
members.description: The bitmap's real width, readable before the element is connected.

members.name: present
members.description:
Paints the current bitmap now; the owner of a `data-manual` canvas calls
this. Returns whether the shaders are still changing the display, so an
owner whose bitmap is static knows when it can stop presenting.

members.name: transition
members.description:
Freezes the frame on show and wipes the frames drawn after it in over it,
blob by blob through a noise mask, so a change of scene dissolves rather
than cuts. The frozen frame is what was shown, styled and mid-dissolve
included, so nothing jumps. Before the first present there is nothing to
freeze, and the next frame shows at once.

members.name: reset
members.description: Drops every pass's state and any dissolve, so the next present shows the bitmap as drawn.

declarations.description:
`<pixel-backdrop>` fills the viewport with a live `<emulated-canvas>`, its
child, and runs a backdrop toy on it. The toy only draws on the canvas and
listens to it, as it would on any canvas; the element picks the toy, styles
the canvas (the display's palette, the drifting noise, the dissolve between
toys), and passes it the pointer. The layer is fixed and non-interactive,
so the page above it paints its own solid panels over the result. Its
layout is `pixel-backdrop.css`, which also holds the knobs' defaults; a
page overrides them on its own `:root`.

The element owns its render knobs, which `configure()` can tweak live.
`resolveLook` turns them, the toy's look and the display into the
`<emulated-canvas>`'s `data-*` attributes, its public API, and the
properties the backdrop's stylesheet reads. Under reduced motion it runs
no toy.
declarations.name: PixelBackdrop

cssProperties.name: --backdrop-ghost

cssProperties.name: --backdrop-noise

members.name: display
members.description:
The screen the toys show on: its palette and, for a physical panel, its
look. Set it before the element is defined, or before its canvas is
attached, and the first frame is already in it; a change later restarts
the canvas's passes when the palette differs.

members.name: toy
members.description: The id of the chosen toy, which is the incoming one mid-dissolve.

members.name: knobs
members.description:
The knobs in effect for the chosen toy on the display. A display's own
ghost rise and fall are not among them.

members.name: tweaks
members.description: A copy of the knobs set through `configure` since the last `reset`.

members.name: configure
members.description: Merge a partial set of knobs, and repaint.

members.name: reset
members.description: Restore the defaults from the `--backdrop-*` custom properties, and drop every tweak.

members.name: setToy
members.description:
Dissolve into a registered toy, starting it fresh; an unknown id is
ignored, and so is the toy already chosen. A request while no toy runs
(before the canvas exists, disabled, reduced motion) is remembered and
starts when one can.

members.name: play
members.description: Like `setToy` for a toy the registry does not list.

declarations.summary: A fixed, viewport-filling pixel grid that runs an interactive canvas toy.
